nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard accrual-based commercial expenses from statutory liabilities requiring actual cash outflow or timely return-filing payment.

path.name: SURPLUS ON SALE OF SHARES AND SECURITIES - WHETHER TAXABLE AS CAPITAL GAINS OR BUSINESS INCOME? [CIRCULAR NO. 06/2016, DATED 29-2-2016]
Characterization of Surplus on Sale of Shares and Securities

exclusion: Personal assets subject to statutory exceptions
inclusion: Listed shares
Securities held as capital assets
Securities held as stock-in-trade
descriptor.definition: The characterization of surplus from the sale of shares and securities as either capital gains or business income depends on whether the assets are held as investments or stock-in-trade. This determination relies on factual circumstances, taxpayer intent, and established judicial and regulatory principles.
source_ambiguities: The source text truncates at the end, cutting off the specific sub-clauses for assessing stock-in-trade options.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between investment holdings yielding capital gains and trading assets yielding business income.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO INCOME OF POLITICAL PARTIES AND ELECTORAL TRUSTS [SECTION 12]
Special Provisions Relating to Income of Political Parties and Electoral Trusts

exclusion: Income failing to meet record-keeping and audit criteria
Donations accepted outside prescribed banking or electronic channels beyond permitted limits
inclusion: Income from house property of political parties
Voluntary contributions received by political parties and electoral trusts
Capital gains and income from other sources for political bodies
descriptor.definition: Political parties and electoral trusts receive tax exemptions on specific categories of income such as house property, other sources, capital gains, and voluntary contributions. To claim this exemption, entities must maintain proper books of accounts, record large contributions, audit accounts via a chartered accountant, and file required statutory returns.
nearby_distinctions: Exempts political and electoral income only upon strict compliance with transparency and record-keeping mandates, unlike standard trust income.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS IN RESPECT OF SLUMP SALE [SECTION 77]
Capital Gains in Respect of Slump Sale

exclusion: Transfer of individual assets or liabilities not constituting an active business undertaking
inclusion: Transfer of an entire undertaking, division, or business activity for a lump sum
Assets held for more than 36 months taxed as long-term and 36 months or less as short-term
descriptor.definition: A slump sale involves transferring one or more undertakings for a lump sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets and liabilities. The net worth of the undertaking is deemed the cost of acquisition and improvement, while the fair market value serves as the full value of consideration.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from itemized asset sales because individual asset valuation is absent, utilizing undertaking net worth instead.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
Stamp Duty Value of Stock-in-Trade as Consideration

exclusion: Transfers where stamp duty value is within 110 percent of actual consideration
inclusion: Land or buildings held as non-capital assets
Transfers where consideration falls below stamp duty value threshold
descriptor.definition: When land or building held as stock-in-trade is transferred for an amount less than its stamp duty value, that stamp duty value is deemed to be the full value of consideration. However, if the stamp duty value does not exceed 110 percent of the actual consideration received, the actual consideration applies.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from capital asset property transfers by specific application to stock-in-trade inventory holdings.

exclusion: Returns filed after the expiry of the belated filing deadline
inclusion: Returns submitted after the section 139(1) due date within permitted statutory windows
descriptor.definition: A belated return is filed by any person who missed the original due date, submitted prior to three months before the end of the assessment year or before assessment completion. Filing a belated return incurs interest, late fees, and restrictions on carrying forward certain losses or claiming specific deductions.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike original timely returns, belated returns restrict loss carry-forward privileges and strip eligibility for specific tax incentive deductions.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment of tax and defaults by the assessee [Section 220]
Payment of tax and defaults by the assessee [Section 220]

exclusion: Penalty levy mechanisms
Recovery proceedings through TRO
inclusion: Demand payments within thirty days
Interest on unpaid dues
Reduction or increase of interest resulting from rectification or appellate orders
descriptor.definition: Amounts specified in a notice of demand must be paid within thirty days of service, though the Assessing Officer may extend time, permit installments, or shorten the period if revenue is endangered. Failure to pay within this period triggers simple interest liability for every month or part of a month of default.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 221 penalties as it deals strictly with statutory payment timelines and compounding interest rather than penal impositions for defaults.

exclusion: Incomes subject to special tax rates under independent statutory sections
inclusion: Concessional tax rates under default regimes
Surcharge on higher income thresholds
Health and Education Cess at four percent
descriptor.definition: Income-tax liability is computed using specified tax rates, augmented by a surcharge levied as a percentage of tax beyond specific income thresholds. Additionally, a Health and Education Cess is applied to the combined total of income-tax and surcharge for all assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between base tax rates, progressive surcharges, and the universal health and education cess.

path.name: Tax Treatment and Cost Adjustment for Advance Money Received

exclusion: Advances received and forfeited by a previous owner rather than the current assessee
inclusion: Advance money retained following the breakdown of asset transfer negotiations
Advances forfeited before 1st April 2014 for cost reduction purposes
descriptor.definition: Advance money received during negotiations for a capital asset that is subsequently forfeited must be deducted from the cost of acquisition, written down value, or fair market value unless it has been taxed as income under specific provisions. Advances forfeited on or after 1st April 2014 are taxable under income from other sources, preventing double taxation through cost deductions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by timing; advances forfeited before 1-4-2014 reduce acquisition cost, whereas later forfeitures are taxed separately as other income.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS TAXATION FOR NON RESIDENTS

exclusion: Indexation benefits for transfers on or after specific statutory dates
inclusion: Capital gains from transfer of Indian company shares or debentures acquired in foreign exchange
Conversion using applicable telegraphic transfer rates
descriptor.definition: Non-residents transferring capital assets in India are subject to capital gains tax, with specific currency fluctuation benefits applied when foreign exchange is invested. Computations require converting consideration, acquisition cost, and transfer expenses into the initial foreign currency used before reconverting the resulting gain into Indian currency.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard domestic capital gains calculation from foreign currency fluctuation adjusted calculations

path.name: Exemptions for US 64 Units and Compulsory Acquisition of Agricultural Land

exclusion: Voluntary sales of agricultural land not governed by compulsory acquisition laws or government approvals
inclusion: Income from transfer of US 64 units on or after 1.4.2002
Compensation from compulsory acquisition of specified urban agricultural land held by individuals or HUFs
descriptor.definition: Capital gains arising from the transfer of Unit Scheme 1964 units are exempt from tax. Similarly, capital gains derived by individuals or Hindu Undivided Families from the compulsory acquisition of urban agricultural land used for farming are exempt under specified conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from regular taxable capital gains by providing complete statutory exemption based on asset type and acquisition context.

path.name: TAX ON SHORT TERM CAPITAL GAINS IN RESPECT OF EQUITY SHARES/ UNITS OF AN EQUITY ORIENTED FUND/ UNITS OF A BUSINESS TRUST [SECTION 196]
Tax on Short-Term Capital Gains on Specified Securities

exclusion: Short-term capital gains not subject to securities transaction tax except specified IFSC transactions
inclusion: Equity shares in a company
Units of an equity-oriented fund
Units of a business trust
descriptor.definition: Short-term capital gains arising from the transfer of equity shares, equity-oriented fund units, or business trust units are chargeable at a concessional rate of 20 percent if subject to securities transaction tax. Resident individuals and HUFs can adjust unexhausted basic exemption limits against these gains.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from ordinary short-term capital gains by offering a flat concessional tax rate and allowing basic exemption adjustments for residents.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]

exclusion: individuals and HUFs required to deduct tax under Sections 194C, 194H, or 194J
inclusion: contract work payments
commission or brokerage
fees for professional services made by non-audit individuals and HUFs
descriptor.definition: Individuals and HUFs not subject to regular business audit requirements who pay substantial sums for contract work, commission, brokerage, or professional services must deduct tax at source. Taxpayers already obligated to deduct tax under specific contractor, commission, or professional sections are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as a catch-all provision for individual and HUF payees who exceed high financial thresholds but lack business audit obligations.

path.name: Charging Provision and Scope of Capital Gains

exclusion: Stock-in-trade held for business or profession
Consumable stores
Raw materials held for business
inclusion: Property of any kind held by an assessee
Securities held by specified Foreign Institutional Investors or investment funds
Unit linked insurance policies without specific exemptions
descriptor.definition: Profits and gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset effected in a tax year are chargeable to income-tax under the head Capital Gains and deemed as income of that specific year. The core elements driving this charge are the identification of a valid capital asset and a recognized transfer.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between items held as business stock-in-trade versus items held as personal investments based on the manner of holding rather than the inherent nature of the asset.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits on a presumptive basis unless claiming lower than deemed profits
inclusion: Businesses with total sales or turnover exceeding 1 crore or 10 crore depending on cash transaction proportions
Professionals with gross receipts exceeding 50 lakhs
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professionals must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date if their turnover or gross receipts exceed statutory monetary limits. An audit report in the prescribed form must be duly signed and verified.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general maintenance of books of account by requiring formal verification and reporting by an external accountant.

path.name: Chapter 11: Tax Planning, Tax Avoidance and Tax Evasion
TAX PLANNING, TAX AVOIDANCE AND TAX EVASION – AN OVERVIEW
Tax Planning, Tax Avoidance and Tax Evasion Overview

exclusion: Illegal suppression of income
Fraudulent manipulation of accounts
inclusion: Application of tax law provisions to practical situations
Utilization of statutory exemptions and deductions
Analysis of CBDT circulars and court case laws
descriptor.definition: Tax planning involves arranging financial affairs to minimize tax liability by fully utilizing available exemptions, deductions, and reliefs without violating any legal provisions. It requires a thorough understanding of direct tax laws, judicial pronouncements, and CBDT circulars to optimize investible surplus.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from tax evasion by operating strictly within legal boundaries rather than through illegal concealment or fraud.

path.name: MONETARY LIMITS FOR REGULATING FILING OF APPEALS BY INCOME TAX AUTHORITIES [SECTION 268A]
Monetary Limits for Regulating Filing of Appeals by Income Tax Authorities

exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
descriptor.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

exclusion: Original receipts that never received prior expense or loss write-off deductions
inclusion: Subsequent cash receipts compensating for prior allowed losses or expenditures
Benefits derived from previously written-off trading liabilities
descriptor.definition: Recoveries or benefits derived from previously allowed deductions for losses, expenditures, or trading liabilities are treated as taxable income. This deemed income is taxable in the financial year in which the amount is received or the benefit accrues.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary income generation events from secondary recoveries of previously claimed expense deductions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]

exclusion: benefits or perquisites to a resident where aggregate value does not exceed 20,000 rupees in a financial year
providers being individuals or HUFs whose business turnover or professional receipts do not exceed statutory thresholds
inclusion: benefits or perquisites arising from business or exercise of a profession
perquisites provided wholly in kind, partly in kind, or in cash
descriptor.definition: Any person providing business or professional benefits or perquisites to a resident must ensure tax is deducted at source before release, regardless of whether the benefit is in cash, kind, or partly both. If the benefit is wholly or partly in kind and available cash is insufficient to cover tax, the deductor must ensure tax is paid prior to release.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard monetary income TDS by capturing non-monetary or mixed business advantages provided to trade partners or professionals.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Capital receipts generally excluded from business income computations
inclusion: Profits realized in cash or in kind
Single trade ventures if undertaken with profit intent
Vocations included under professional scope
descriptor.definition: Business encompasses trade, commerce, manufacture, or any trade adventure pursued with a profit motive, whereas profession denotes occupations requiring specialized learning and includes vocations. Profits from both categories are generally taxable under the same head, while differences persist primarily for tax audit and presumptive taxation thresholds.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between continuous commercial operations and isolated trade adventures, and differentiates traditional businesses from learned professions.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
Mandatory Tax Audit Provisions and Thresholds

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits in accordance with section 44AD(1) or 44ADA(1)
inclusion: Businesses with total sales exceeding specific statutory limits
Professions with gross receipts exceeding fifty lakh rupees
Assessees claiming lower profits than presumptive rates under designated sections
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professions must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date when financial metrics cross prescribed monetary thresholds. Exceptions and specific conditions regarding cash receipts and payments apply to business turnovers within defined limits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes business turnover thresholds from professional gross receipt thresholds and presumptive income reporting rules.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
PENALTY FOR FAILURE TO FURNISH TAX AUDIT REPORT [SECTION 271B]
Penalty for Failure to Furnish Tax Audit Report under Section 271B

exclusion: Instances where a valid reasonable cause for default is successfully proved under section 273B
inclusion: Penalties for non-compliance with tax audit submission mandates
Aggregation rules for multiple business turnovers when evaluating thresholds
descriptor.definition: Failure to complete accounts audits or submit required tax audit reports under section 44AB attracts a monetary penalty levied by the Assessing Officer. The penalty amount is calculated as a specified percentage of total turnover or gross receipts, subject to a statutory ceiling, unless a reasonable cause is proven.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general income tax default penalties by specifically targeting the omission of mandatory tax audit reports.

path.name: TAX ON LONG TERM CAPITAL GAINS [SECTION 197]
Taxation and Indexation of Long-Term Capital Gains

exclusion: Short-term capital gains and assets governed by special equity taxation sections
inclusion: Long-term capital assets other than those under section 198
Land or buildings acquired before 23.7.2024 for resident individuals and HUFs
descriptor.definition: Long-term capital gains on general assets are taxable at a concessional rate of 12.5 percent, with resident individuals and HUFs permitted to absorb unexhausted basic exemption limits. Specific indexation benefits apply to land or buildings acquired before a designated threshold date.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from section 198 assets by applying to broader long-term asset categories and incorporating potential indexation adjustments for older real estate.

path.name: DEEMED FULL VALUE OF CONSIDERATION FOR COMPUTING CAPITAL GAINS [SECTION 78, 79 & 80]
Deemed Full Value of Consideration for Land or Building

exclusion: Transactions where the stamp duty value is within 110 percent of the actual sale consideration
inclusion: Transfer of land, buildings, or both
Transactions where stamp duty value exceeds 110 percent of actual proceeds
descriptor.definition: When land or buildings are transferred at a consideration lower than the stamp duty value, the stamp duty value is deemed to be the full value of consideration if it exceeds 110 percent of the actual consideration. Special alignment rules apply when the agreement date and registration date differ and consideration is paid through specified banking or online modes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard sales where actual consideration received is taken, applying statutory substitution only when thresholds are breached.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices
Penalties for Foreign Income and Asset Non-Compliance

exclusion: Low-value bank accounts and minor aggregate asset holdings within statutory monetary limits
inclusion: Penalties equal to three times the tax computed
Fixed sum penalties for omission of foreign asset information
descriptor.definition: Assessees face financial penalties amounting to multiples of computed tax or fixed monetary fines for failing to disclose foreign assets or file required returns. Specific monetary thresholds and asset types provide exemptions from these penalties under defined conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from prosecution as these represent administrative financial sanctions rather than criminal imprisonment offenses.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS ON DISTRIBUTION OF ASSETS BY COMPANIES IN LIQUIDATION [SECTION 68]
Capital Gains on Distribution of Assets by Companies in Liquidation

exclusion: Distribution events treated as company transfers when liquidators sell assets directly prior to distribution
inclusion: Shareholder capital gains on money or assets received during company liquidation
Fair market value adoption as cost of acquisition for subsequent asset sales by shareholders
descriptor.definition: Asset distributions by a liquidated company to its shareholders are not treated as transfers at the company level, while shareholders face capital gains tax based on the market value of received assets minus accumulated profit components. Portions of distributions attributable to accumulated profits are treated separately as dividend income under other income sources.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes company-level exemption from asset distribution against shareholder-level taxation which splits distributions into deemed dividends and capital gains.

path.name: APPLICABLE RATE OF TAX IN RESPECT OF WINNINGS FROM ONLINE GAMES [SECTION 194(1) (TABLE: SI. NO. 5)]

exclusion: Traditional physical lotteries, crosswords, and offline gambling winnings
inclusion: Net winnings originating from internet-accessible games via computer resources
descriptor.definition: Net winnings from online games accessed through computer resources or telecommunication devices are subject to a flat tax rate. No related expenditure allowances, Chapter VIII deductions, or basic exemption limit adjustments are permitted against this income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes digital and internet-based gaming platforms from traditional offline casual income sources.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: Setting off capital gains losses against any other head
Setting off business losses against salary income
inclusion: Adjusting business losses against other heads except salaries
Setting off house property loss up to specified monetary limits against other heads under the default regime
descriptor.definition: Losses computed under one head of income may be adjusted against income under another head within the same tax year, excluding capital gains. Specific restrictions apply, such as business losses not being adjustable against salary income and house property losses being capped or restricted depending on the tax regime.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes inter-head adjustments from inter-source adjustments restricted strictly within the same head.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]

exclusion: transactions subject to tax deduction under other provisions where section 194Q priority rules apply
transactions liable to TCS under specific sub-sections of section 206C
inclusion: sum paid or credited for purchasing goods exceeding 50 lakhs rupees in a previous year
buyers with business turnover exceeding 10 crores rupees in the preceding financial year
descriptor.definition: Large business buyers whose preceding financial year turnover exceeds specified monetary limits must deduct tax at source when purchasing goods from a resident seller exceeding aggregate thresholds. The deduction occurs at the time of credit to the seller's account or actual payment, whichever happens earlier.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from TCS provisions under section 206C(1H) by placing the compliance burden directly on the high-turnover buyer rather than the seller.

exclusion: Requiring accounts relating to a period more than 3 years prior to the previous year
inclusion: Issuance of notice to furnish returns
Production of accounts and documents
Submission of written information on assets and liabilities
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer may serve a notice to require a return, production of accounts and documents, or written information regarding assets and liabilities. Account production is restricted to periods not exceeding three years prior to the previous year, and asset statements require joint commissioner approval.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from summary processing under section 143(1) by involving active inquiries, document production demands, and notices issued directly by tax authorities.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Basic interest computations for delayed tax payments under Section 220
inclusion: Penalties for tax or advance tax default
Cancellation of penalty if the underlying tax demand is wholly reduced on appeal
descriptor.definition: When an assessee defaults in paying tax, advance tax, or interest, the Assessing Officer shall impose a monetary penalty after providing a reasonable opportunity of being heard, provided no good and sufficient reason is proven. Subsequent payment of the tax in arrears before penalty imposition does not absolve the assessee from this liability.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike routine interest charged automatically under Section 220, Section 221 imposes a punitive charge requiring a hearing and subjective evaluation of good and sufficient reasons.

path.name: PROVISIONAL ATTACHMENT TO PROTECT THE INTEREST OF THE REVENUE [SECTION 281B]
Provisional Attachment To Protect The Interest Of The Revenue [Section 281B]

exclusion: Extensions exceeding a total period of two years or sixty days after assessment/reassessment, whichever is later
inclusion: Provisional attachment of property during pending assessment or reassessment
Attachments for anticipated penalty under section 271AAD exceeding two crore rupees
Revocation of attachment upon furnishing a scheduled bank guarantee
descriptor.definition: Assessing officers are empowered to provisionally attach an assessee's property during pending assessment, reassessment, or penalty proceedings with high-ranking administrative approval to protect revenue interests. Such attachments remain valid for six months, extendable up to two years or sixty days post-assessment, but can be revoked if the assessee furnishes a scheduled bank guarantee.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a precautionary attachment mechanism during active proceedings, distinct from Section 281 which retroactively voids fraudulent transfers

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Taxpayers not meeting statutory income or turnover thresholds and not carrying on specified professions
inclusion: Specified professions like legal, medical, and engineering
Businesses exceeding specified income or turnover limits in preceding years
descriptor.definition: Specified professionals and general business taxpayers meeting specific income or turnover thresholds must maintain accounting records and documents to facilitate income computation by the Assessing Officer. These records can be kept in written, electronic, digital, cloud-based, or printed formats.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from tax audit requirements by focusing on day-to-day record keeping rather than formal chartered accountant verification.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax by a specified bank in case of specified senior citizen [Section 194P]
Deduction of tax by a specified bank in case of specified senior citizen [Section 194P]

exclusion: senior citizens with income sources outside of pension and interest from the specified bank
individuals failing to submit the prescribed verification declaration
inclusion: resident individuals aged 75 years or more receiving pension and interest income from the same bank
total income computed after Chapter VI-A deductions and section 87A rebates
descriptor.definition: Specified scheduled banks are mandated to compute and deduct tax at source on the total income of resident senior citizens aged 75 years or older who maintain pension and interest income within the same bank. This mechanism relieves eligible senior citizens from the statutory obligation of filing an annual income tax return.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular employer salary TDS by placing deduction responsibility directly on designated banks for elderly taxpayers with restricted income profiles.

path.name: POWER OF ASSESSING OFFICER TO MAKE A REFERENCE TO THE VALUATION OFFICER [SECTION 142A]
Power Of Assessing Officer To Make A Reference To The Valuation Officer [Section 142A]

exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Components of Defined Benefit Cost and Net Interest

exclusion: Reclassification of OCI remeasurements into profit or loss during subsequent accounting periods
inclusion: Service costs recognized in profit or loss unless capitalized under specific standards
Net interest calculated using opening or remeasured discount rates
descriptor.definition: Defined benefit costs comprise service costs and net interest recognized in profit or loss, alongside remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income. Net interest is determined by multiplying the net defined benefit liability or asset by the specified discount rate.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes operating service and financing interest components routed through profit or loss from volatile actuarial remeasurements isolated in other comprehensive income.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Definitions relating to defined benefit cost
Definitions Relating To Defined Benefit Cost

exclusion: Standard administrative costs of managing general corporate operations
inclusion: Current period service increases
Impact of plan amendments and curtailments
Actuarial experience adjustments and assumption changes
descriptor.definition: Defined benefit cost comprises service cost, net interest on the net defined benefit liability or asset, and remeasurements. Service cost includes current service cost, past service cost from plan amendments, and gains or losses on settlements.
nearby_distinctions: Isolates the time-value interest component and actuarial volatility from standard operational service expenses.

exclusion: Grants without reasonable assurance of compliance or receipt
inclusion: Monetary grants
Non-monetary grants at fair value
descriptor.definition: Government grants are recognized only when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will comply with attached conditions and that the grant will be received. Mere physical receipt of funds does not automatically constitute conclusive evidence of condition fulfillment.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from cash-basis recognition by requiring the dual threshold of condition compliance assurance and receipt likelihood.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: General business terms outside accounting standards
inclusion: Key defined terms governing intangible asset accounting
descriptor.definition: This section provides core terminology for applying the standard, defining parameters such as amortisation, carrying amount, cost, development, and fair value. These definitions establish the structural basis for recognizing and measuring intangible items.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes entity-specific value from fair value and monetary assets from non-monetary assets.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Unit 5: THE ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
LINK BETWEEN INFORMATION IN GENERAL PURPOSE FINANCIAL REPORTS AS PER CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Link Between Information In General Purpose Financial Reports As Per Conceptual Framework And Elements Of Financial Statements

exclusion: Equity contributions and distributions categorized as financial performance elements
inclusion: Mapping of economic resources to assets and claims to liabilities
Mapping of financial changes to income and expense elements
descriptor.definition: General purpose financial reports reflect underlying economic resources and claims through specific balance sheet elements like assets, liabilities, and equity. Changes in these resources and claims over time are captured via financial performance elements such as income and expenses.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes static structural elements (assets, liabilities, equity) from dynamic performance elements (income, expenses).

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Reimbursements and Defined Benefit Cost Components

exclusion: Reclassification of OCI remeasurements back to profit or loss in subsequent periods
inclusion: Separate asset recognition for non-qualifying insurance policy reimbursements
Non-reclassifiable remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income
descriptor.definition: An entity recognizes a right to reimbursement as a separate asset only when recovery from a third party is virtually certain. Defined benefit costs are parsed into service costs, net interest, and remeasurements, with remeasurements recognized entirely in other comprehensive income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes third-party insurer reimbursements from internal plan assets by requiring separate asset presentation unless tied to a qualifying insurance policy.

exclusion: Standard commercial loans at prevailing market rates
inclusion: Loan forgiveness terms
Interest differential calculations
descriptor.definition: Forgivable loans from governments convert to grants when there is reasonable assurance the entity will satisfy forgiveness terms. Below-market interest rate loans derive a government grant component measured as the difference between initial fair value under financial instrument standards and proceeds received.
nearby_distinctions: Below-market loans split into a financial liability measured at fair value and a deferred grant benefit.

exclusion: fixed-price equity-settled instruments lacking cash settlement mechanisms
inclusion: share appreciation rights settled in cash
variable bonuses based on share prices without vesting periods
descriptor.definition: Cash-settled transactions require measuring goods, services, and resulting liabilities at the liability fair value. Entities must remeasure the liability fair value at each reporting date until settlement, recognizing any fair value adjustments directly in profit or loss.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from equity-settled plans by ongoing liability remeasurement through profit or loss rather than fixed equity accounting.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income for post-employment benefits
inclusion: Service cost components
Net interest on net defined benefit liability or asset
Remeasurements in profit or loss
descriptor.definition: Entities recognize the net total of service cost, net interest, and remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability or asset in profit or loss. Obligations for long-term disability depend on service duration and payment probabilities, or trigger upon the disabling event.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from post-employment benefit accounting by routing remeasurements directly to profit or loss instead of other comprehensive income.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Definitions relating to the net defined benefit liability (asset)
Definitions Relating To The Net Defined Benefit Liability (Asset)

exclusion: Non-transferable financial instruments issued by the reporting entity itself
inclusion: Funds held in legally separate long-term employee benefit entities
Insurance policies issued by unrelated parties dedicated to funding benefits
descriptor.definition: Net defined benefit liability or asset is the plan deficit or surplus adjusted for any asset ceiling limits. Plan assets and qualifying insurance policies are measured at fair value to offset the present value of the defined benefit obligation.
terminology: Present Value of Defined Benefit Obligation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general corporate assets and restricted plan assets unavailable to general creditors.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: single measurement basis applied uniformly without separation
inclusion: interest-bearing financial assets measured at fair value through OCI
separation of total fair value changes
descriptor.definition: Multiple measurement bases may be necessary when using a single basis fails to faithfully represent both financial position and performance. Total current value changes can be separated so that profit or loss reflects one basis while other comprehensive income captures the remainder.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from single-basis reporting by segregating performance impacts between profit or loss and OCI.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Accounting treatment on loss of control of a subsidiary
Accounting treatment on loss of control of a subsidiary

exclusion: Transactions where control is maintained by the parent group
inclusion: Fair value recognition of retained financial assets or investments in associates
Recycling of related comprehensive income components
descriptor.definition: When control is lost, the parent derecognizes the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, and non-controlling interest, and brings any retained investment onto the books at fair value. The resulting net difference is recognized as a gain or loss in profit or loss alongside reclassified amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from intra-group reorganizations where assets remain under ultimate parent control.

exclusion: Fixed equity adjustments
inclusion: Periodic liability revaluations
Cash settlement tracking
descriptor.definition: Cash-settled share-based payment liabilities are initially recognized and subsequently fair-valued at the end of each reporting period until final settlement is achieved. Changes in the fair value of the liability are recognized directly in the statement of profit and loss.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike equity-settled plans that keep fair value fixed at grant date, cash-settled plans revalue the liability continuously.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Unit 6: IND AS 28: INVESTMENTS IN ASSOCIATES AND JOINT
DISCONTINUING THE USE OF THE EQUITY METHOD
Discontinuing The Use Of The Equity Method

exclusion: continued application of the equity method when joint control or significant influence persists
retaining historical carrying amounts without fair value adjustment for retained financial assets
inclusion: measurement of retained interest at fair value
recognition of gain or loss on partial disposal and discontinuation in profit or loss
descriptor.definition: An entity must stop applying the equity method when its investment ceases to qualify as an associate or a joint venture. Any retained interest is then accounted for as a financial asset measured at fair value, with differences recognized in profit or loss.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from business combinations where previously held interests are revalued upon gaining control versus discontinuation resulting in financial asset classification.

exclusion: Monetary grants
Loans provided by government at market rates
inclusion: Transfers of land at nominal or concessional values
Transfers of non-monetary resources for entity use
descriptor.definition: Non-monetary government grants involve transfers of resources such as land or assets provided to an entity at a concessional rate or free of charge. Entities can record both the asset and the grant either at their assessed fair value or alternatively at a nominal value.
nearby_distinctions: Monetary grants are received in cash equivalents, whereas non-monetary grants involve physical or intangible resources transferred directly.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Unallocated corporate asset impairments lacking segment attribution
inclusion: Segment-level impairment losses
Segment-level impairment reversals
descriptor.definition: Entities reporting segment information under Ind AS 108 must disclose impairment losses and reversals recognized in both profit or loss and other comprehensive income for each reportable segment. This ensures visibility of impairment trends across business segments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from entity-wide class disclosures by segregating financial figures strictly according to reportable operating segments.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Consequences of losing control of a subsidiary during the reporting period
Consequences of Losing Control of a Subsidiary During the Reporting Period

exclusion: Intra-group reorganizations where consolidated control is preserved
inclusion: Portion of gain or loss from fair value remeasurement of retained stakes
Profit or loss presentation line items
descriptor.definition: When control over a subsidiary ceases, the entity must disclose the resulting net gain or loss computation. Additionally, it must specify the portion of the gain or loss attributable to remeasuring any retained investment at fair value alongside its income statement line item location.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on terminal deconsolidation reporting rather than interim ownership fluctuations.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: General operational depreciation and amortisation expenses
inclusion: Impairment losses and reversals recognised in profit or loss
Impairment losses and reversals recognised in other comprehensive income
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose financial statement line items, amounts, and comprehensive details regarding impairment losses and reversals across asset classes and segments. These disclosures provide transparency regarding the financial impact of asset impairments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard depreciation disclosures by focusing explicitly on abnormal downward revaluations and recoveries.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Segment-specific reporting disclosures handled separately
inclusion: Impairment losses and reversals by asset class
descriptor.definition: Entities are required to disclose class-specific impairment losses and reversals recognized in profit or loss and other comprehensive income during the reporting period. This information may be integrated within standard asset class reconciliations such as property, plant, and equipment schedules.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from material event disclosures by focusing on aggregated class-level totals rather than specific individual loss events.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Calculation of goodwill / capital reserve when the interest in subsidiary is acquired on different dates (i.e. step acquisition)

exclusion: Adjustments where control was already held prior to the additional stake purchase
inclusion: Remeasurement of prior non-controlling stakes upon obtaining control
Recognition of gain or loss in profit or loss
descriptor.definition: In a business combination achieved in stages, the acquirer must remeasure its previously held equity interest at fair value on the acquisition date. Any resulting gain or loss is recognized directly in profit or loss or other comprehensive income as appropriate.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from single-date acquisitions where no pre-existing equity interest requires fair value remeasurement through profit or loss.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Contributions due for the period without actuarial valuation
inclusion: Unfunded and funded defined benefit plans
Actuarial estimations of demographic and financial variables
descriptor.definition: Defined benefit plans involve estimating employee benefits earned in current and prior periods using actuarial techniques and discounting them to present value. The resulting obligation is adjusted by deducting the fair value of plan assets to determine any net deficit or surplus.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from defined contribution plans where an entity's obligation is strictly limited to the amount it agrees to contribute to the fund.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 10: EVENTS AFTER THE REPORTING PERIOD
Accounting Principles enunciated by Appendix A to Ind AS 10
Accounting Principles enunciated by Appendix A to Ind AS 10

exclusion: Direct recognition of settlement differences inside equity reserves
inclusion: Liability recognition upon authorization
Fair value measurement of non-cash distributions
Profit or loss recognition of settlement variances
descriptor.definition: Entities must recognize dividend liabilities upon authorization when discretion is removed, measuring non-cash distributions at fair value with ongoing period adjustments routed through equity. Any difference between distributed asset carrying amounts and dividend liability values upon settlement is recognized directly in profit or loss.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity transactions by requiring settlement variances to pass through profit or loss as a separate line item rather than modifying equity balances directly.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Profit or loss and other comprehensive income
Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income

exclusion: permanent omission of performance items from financial statements
inclusion: inclusion of performance items in profit or loss
exceptional allocation of current value changes to other comprehensive income
descriptor.definition: All income and expenses are included in profit or loss unless exceptional standard-setting permits inclusion in other comprehensive income. Items in other comprehensive income may subsequently be reclassified into profit or loss when relevant.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary performance reporting in profit or loss from items routed through other comprehensive income.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 21 : THE EFFECTS OF CHANGES IN FOREIGN
Recognition of foreign exchange gains and losses
Recognition of Foreign Exchange Gains and Losses

exclusion: Standard translation of foreign operations presented in separate equity reserves
Unsettled long-term monetary items with specific equity recognition elections
inclusion: Exchange differences on monetary settlements recognized in profit or loss
Cash flow hedge exchange differences recognized in other comprehensive income
Exchange components of non-monetary asset revaluations processed through other comprehensive income
descriptor.definition: Exchange differences arising from settlement or translation of monetary items are recognized in profit or loss, except when specific hedge accounting or net investment rules apply. For non-monetary items, any exchange component follows the primary gain or loss recognition path, whether in profit or loss or other comprehensive income.
nearby_distinctions: Monetary exchange differences default to profit or loss unless bound by specific hedging or net investment exceptions, unlike non-monetary exchange items that shadow the underlying asset's destination.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability (asset)
Remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability (asset)

exclusion: Past service cost
Gains or losses on settlement
Current service cost
Net interest on net defined benefit liability
inclusion: Actuarial gains and losses from assumption changes
Experience adjustments
Return on plan assets excluding net interest components
Changes in asset ceiling effect excluding net interest
descriptor.definition: Remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability or asset comprise actuarial gains and losses, the return on plan assets excluding amounts included in net interest, and changes in the effect of the asset ceiling excluding net interest amounts. Actuarial gains and losses arise from changes in actuarial assumptions and experience adjustments in measuring the defined benefit obligation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from past service costs which stem from plan amendments or curtailments rather than demographic or financial assumption variances.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Disconnecting tax accounting from the classification of the underlying economic event
inclusion: Tax effects recognized in profit or loss, OCI, or equity
Pro rata allocation for complex items recognized outside profit or loss
descriptor.definition: The accounting treatment for deferred tax effects must align with the underlying transaction or event, being recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or directly in equity. Subsequent changes in deferred tax balances driven by tax rate changes are also routed through profit or loss unless tied to prior non-P&L items.
nearby_distinctions: Items originating in equity or OCI mandate that their corresponding deferred tax adjustments bypass the statement of profit and loss.

path.name: Financial Statements of Corporate Entities under Schedule III

exclusion: Horizontal balance sheet formats
Prescription of specific accounting measurement treatments
inclusion: Vertical balance sheet formatting
Minimum face-value disclosures and note disclosures
descriptor.definition: Corporate financial statements must follow the vertical format and minimum disclosure requirements set out in Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013. Schedule III prescribes content and presentation rules but does not dictate underlying accounting treatments, which are governed by notified standards.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard-setting rules because Schedule III governs presentation formats rather than the accounting recognition and measurement principles.
instrument_references: Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013

path.name: Grant for expenses or losses already incurred and grant as an immediate financial support
Grants for Past Expenses and Non-Monetary Valuations

exclusion: Grants tied to future expenditure obligations
inclusion: Compensation for prior losses
Fair value or nominal asset recording
descriptor.definition: Grants acting as compensation for past expenses or immediate financial support without future cost obligations are recognized directly in profit or loss when receivable. Non-monetary asset transfers are measured at fair value or nominal value with equivalent deferred income setup.
nearby_distinctions: Immediate recognition applies when no further performance obligations or future costs remain.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Attributing benefit to periods of service
Attributing Benefit to Periods of Service

exclusion: Attribution models failing to adjust for disproportionate benefit surges in later working years
inclusion: Obligations arising from employee service even prior to formal vesting
Discounted present values reflecting expected employee departure dates
descriptor.definition: Entities attribute benefits to service periods based on the plan's formula, utilizing straight-line allocation if later service yields materially higher benefits. This attribution spans from the initial date service leads to benefits until further service yields no material benefit increases outside of salary adjustments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard period-cost matching by linking the liability creation directly to historical and current employee service delivery.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Objective and Scope of Ind AS 19

exclusion: Share-based payment transactions under Ind AS 102
Reporting by employee benefit plans themselves
inclusion: Formal employee benefit plans
Statutory or industry arrangement contributions
Informal practices creating constructive obligations
descriptor.definition: The standard prescribes accounting and disclosure for employee benefits, requiring entities to recognize a liability for services received and an expense when economic benefits are consumed. Accrual accounting principles govern these obligations so that employment costs are recorded in the periods corresponding to the services rendered.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike equity transactions with owners, employee benefits are operating expenses reflecting consumption of services.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: Owner transactions in equity
inclusion: Interest revenue via effective interest method
Finance costs
Impairment losses
descriptor.definition: The statement of profit and loss must segregate profit or loss and other comprehensive income sections while reporting total comprehensive income. Consolidated versions must further allocate these totals between non-controlling interests and owners of the parent.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from balance sheet positions by summarizing financial performance over a defined temporal interval.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Balance Sheet Recognition of Defined Benefit Obligations

exclusion: Unfunded commitments not assessed through formal present value and plan asset matching
inclusion: Presentation of deficits as non-current liabilities under provisions
Control of resources providing future economic benefits via contribution reductions or cash refunds
descriptor.definition: Entities must recognize the net defined benefit liability or asset directly on the balance sheet. Net defined benefit assets are restricted to the lower of the plan surplus or the asset ceiling determined through discounting.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with standard deferred tax assets that depend strictly on future taxable profit probabilities rather than explicit plan asset trust investments.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITY
EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITY

exclusion: unrecognized informal commitments outside established plan parameters
inclusion: wages, salaries, and bonuses
gratuity plan obligations and actuarial gains and losses
descriptor.definition: Reporting entities disclose specific accounting policies for employee benefits encompassing short-term compensation, defined contribution plans, and defined benefit plans. Obligations for defined benefit gratuity plans are actuarially measured using the projected unit credit method with re-measurements routed through other comprehensive income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general provisions by applying specialized actuarial discounting and specific other comprehensive income recognition rules for post-employment benefits.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”
Presentation and Disclosure of Revenue Contracts

exclusion: Revenue from interest and dividends covered under financial instruments standards
inclusion: Presentation of contract liabilities when payment is received before performance
Presentation of contract assets or receivables when performance precedes payment
Separate presentation of excise duty in the statement of profit and loss
descriptor.definition: An entity presents contracts in the balance sheet as a contract liability, contract asset, or receivable based on the relationship between performance and payment. Any unconditional right to consideration must be presented separately as a receivable.
nearby_distinctions: A contract asset conditions the right to consideration on something other than the passage of time, whereas a receivable represents an unconditional right requiring only the passage of time.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
INFORMATION PROVIDED BY PARTICULAR MEASUREMENT BASES
Information Provided By Particular Measurement Bases

exclusion: Non-financial operational performance metrics
inclusion: Balance sheet carrying amounts across bases
Statement of profit and loss event treatments
descriptor.definition: Selecting a measurement basis requires evaluating the specific nature of the financial information it produces for both the balance sheet and the statement of profit and loss. Different bases handle transaction costs, interest income, and value changes through distinct recognition and expense mechanisms.
nearby_distinctions: Compares balance sheet presentation and income statement volatility generated by historical cost versus current value alternatives.

path.name: PRESENTATION OF GRANTS RELATED TO ASSETS
Presentation Of Grants Related To Assets

exclusion: Grants related strictly to income without asset acquisition
inclusion: Setting up grants as deferred income
Deducting grants from asset cost
descriptor.definition: Government grants related to assets are presented in the balance sheet either by setting up the grant as deferred income or by deducting the grant from the asset carrying amount. Deferred income is recognized in profit or loss systematically over the useful life of the asset.
nearby_distinctions: Grants related to assets focus on capital property acquisition, whereas grants related to income defray periodic operational expenses.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 8 : ACCOUNTING POLICIES, CHANGES IN ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES AND ERRORS
Accounting treatment for applying changes in accounting estimates
Accounting Treatment for Changes in Estimates

exclusion: Retrospective restatement of prior period financial statements
inclusion: Prospective inclusion of estimate effects in profit or loss
Adjustments to asset, liability, or equity carrying amounts in the current period
descriptor.definition: The financial impact of a change in an accounting estimate is recognized prospectively through profit or loss either in the current period alone or across current and future periods. If the change modifies assets, liabilities, or equity items, its effect is recognized directly by adjusting the carrying amount of the related item during the period of change.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from prior period error corrections, which require retrospective restatement rather than prospective current and future period adjustments.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Classification of post-employment Benefit Plans into Defined Contribution Plan vs Defined Benefit Plans
Defined Contribution Plan Versus Defined Benefit Plan

exclusion: State-administered general security frameworks without entity guarantees
inclusion: Plans with fixed contributions
Plans guaranteeing specific benefit formulas or minimum returns
descriptor.definition: Defined contribution plans limit the entity's obligation to predetermined amounts, placing actuarial and investment risks on the employee. Conversely, defined benefit plans oblige the entity to supply agreed benefits, shifting actuarial and investment vulnerabilities directly onto the employer.
nearby_distinctions: Defined contribution shifts market volatility risks to employees, whereas defined benefit retains those financial risks with the reporting entity.

exclusion: Single-tranche business combinations executed entirely on one date
inclusion: Acquisitions of control through multiple sequential purchases
Remeasurement of prior minority or associate stakes at the date control is secured
descriptor.definition: In a step acquisition, control is achieved in stages through a series of separate share purchases over time. Upon obtaining control, the acquirer must remeasure its previously held equity interest at fair value and recognize any resulting gain or loss.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from single-date combinations by requiring valuation adjustments for prior equity holdings

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES IN IND AS 19 VIS-À-VIS AS 15
Significant Differences In Ind As 19 Vis-À-Vis As 15

exclusion: straight-line amortization of past service cost over the average vesting period
inclusion: comparative criteria for employee definition including non-whole-time directors

parts.question_text:
(i)  SA 250 is applicable only on Audit, and not on other Assurance 
engagements. However, NOCLAR is applicable on professional 
accountants in service, and in practice.

parts.label: ii
parts.question_text:
(ii) SA 250 talks of auditor’s responsibilities for laws having direct effect 
on the determination of material amounts and disclosures in the 
financial statements (such as tax and labour laws); and other laws and 
regulations that do not have a direct effect on the determination of the 
amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, but compliance 
with which may be fundamental to the operating aspects of the 
business. NOCLAR, while being alike to SA 250 till this point, is further 
ahead of it in that it takes into account non-compliance that causes 
substantial harm resulting in serious consequences in financial or non-
financial terms.

parts.label: iii
parts.question_text:
(iii)  SA 250 does not define stakeholders. NOCLAR is related to affect of 
non-compliance on investors, creditors, employees as also the general 
public.

parts.label: iv
parts.question_text:
(iv)  As per NOCLAR, in exceptional circumstances, the professional 
accountant might become aware of an imminent breach of a law or 
regulation that would cause substantial harm to investors, creditors, 
employees or the general public. Having first considered whether it 
would be appropriate to discuss the matter with management or those 
charged with governance of the company, the accountant shall 
exercise professional judgment and determine whether to disclose the 
matter immediately to an appropriate authority in order to prevent or 
mitigate the consequences of such imminent breach. If disclosure is 
made, that disclosure is permitted. This provision is not existent in  
SA 250.

audit, CA R observed that there are number of notices received from GST 
Department and Income-tax Department for various issues. Further during 
plant visit, CA R observed that few child labourers are engaged in some of 
the activity. In response to the observation made, CA R followed the 
procedure as envisaged in SA 250, "Consideration of Laws and Regulations 
in an Audit of Financial Statements". According to CA R, the provisions of SA 
250 and the provisions of NOCLAR (Non-Compliance with Laws and 
Regulations) under Revised Code of Ethics are one and the same. Do you 
agree? If not, give your comments. 
(4 Marks)

(a) Going Concern and Significant Uncertainties: As per SRE 2410, “Review 
of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of 
the Entity”, if, as a result of inquiries or other review procedures, a material 
uncertainty relating to an event or condition comes to the auditor’s 
attention that may cast significant doubt on the entity’s ability to continue 
as a going concern, and adequate disclosure is made in the interim financial 
information the auditor modifies the review report by adding an emphasis 
of matter paragraph.  
The auditor may have modified a prior audit or review report by adding an 
emphasis of matter paragraph to highlight a material uncertainty relating 
to an event or condition that may cast significant doubt on the entity’s 
ability to continue as a going concern.  
If a material uncertainty that casts significant doubt about the entity’s 
ability to continue as a going concern is not adequately disclosed in the

In view of above, in the given situation, GAK Limited has compiled the 
interim financial information, as per the Listing agreement requirements 
and submitted to the auditors for their review. CA Reena, has been assigned 
on the engagement to review the interim financial information of GAK 
Limited. CA Reena noticed that GAK Limited has not disclosed any 
information in the interim financial information relating to material 
uncertainties that casts significant doubt about the entity’s ability to 
continue as a going concern. Thus, the auditor should express a qualified 
or adverse conclusion, as appropriate. The report should include specific 
reference to the fact that there is such a material uncertainty. 
If the material uncertainty still exists and adequate disclosure is made in 
the interim financial information, the auditor modifies the review report on 
the current interim financial information by adding a paragraph to highlight 
the continued material uncertainty. If GAK Limited has disclosed 
information relating to material uncertainties, CA Reena, should modify the 
review report by adding an emphasis of matter paragraph.

parts.question_text: (ii)  Specify with reason, whether the following acts can be considered as:

(a)  (i) Club U Travels Private Limited, engaged in the business of travel 
agency remitted substantial amount to Australia as per the information 
collected by the Income-tax department from PTU Bank. The 
department collected documents from PTU Bank, which include Form 
15CB issued by the chartered accountant, list of passengers, copy of 
their passports, date of travel and invoices raised by the foreign party. 
On enquiry from the passengers and verifying their passports, it is 
found that they did not travel abroad on the dates mentioned in the 
documents. On the top of it the passengers also denied there was no 
transaction with Club U Travels Private Limited. 
The Income-tax department concluded that the amounts were remitted 
by the company on the basis of false invoices and for wrong reasons. It 
led to FEMA violations and Form 15CB issued by the chartered 
accountant was a vital document in these transactions. During the six-
month period in question, the chartered accountant had issued 78 
certificates in Form 15CB involving remittances of ` 35 crores for Club 
U Travels Private Limited. 
A representation was given by the concerned CA that he had issued 
Form 15CB based on invoices produced by the company and verifying 
the KYC documents of the signatory to the invoices. His contention was 
that since he was not the statutory auditor of the company, he did not 
examine the books of account before issuing Form 15CB or conduct due 
diligence of its business activities. He had charged ` 2,500 per 
certificate. Mostly, the fees were collected in cash. Some parts of the 
fees were credited to his bank account. 
27 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
FINAL EXAMINATION: MAY 2024 
Can the chartered accountant be held guilty of professional misconduct 
for failure to obtain sufficient information and failure to exercise due 
diligence in discharging the professional responsibilities? 
(6 Marks)

parts.label: a
parts.question_text:
(A)  Tax planning; or (B) Tax management; or (C) Tax evasion. 
1.  Mr. D has FDR with SBI in his name amounting to ` 50 lakhs. He 
gifted this sum of ` 50 lakhs to his son, on 10.04.2023, the date on 
which he attained 18 years of age. The purpose is to shift interest 
income from his hands to his son, so that there may be Zero tax 
implication, since his son has no other income and the total 
interest would be lower than taxable limits for P.Y. 2023-24. 
2.  Mr. Ram's Annual income is ` 49.50 lakhs for A.Y. 2024-25 
excluding commission receivable from ABC Limited. During March 
2024, he earned a commission of ` 6 lakhs from ABC Limited. He 
asked ABC Limited to transfer the commission in his wife's 
account, who is a housewife. He also asked them to deduct TDS in 
her wife's name. He did it so that his total income may not cross  
` 50 lakhs and he can save surcharge on taxes applicable on total 
income exceeding ` 50 lakhs. His wife has no other income.  
     (4 Marks)

parts.label: b
parts.question_text:
(b) A Non-resident Foreign Company entered into contracts with several 
Indian Companies for installation of mobile telephone system and made an 
application to the Board of Advance Rulings, for advance ruling in relation 
to the tax liability arising out of such transaction. 
One of the above said Indian Companies also made an application to its 
Assessing Officer for determination of a question of law with regard to 
payments to be made to the said Foreign Company. 
The Board of Advance Rulings rejected the application of the Foreign 
Company on the ground that the question raised is pending before an 
Income Tax Authority. Is the rejection of the application of the Foreign 
Company justified in law? 
(4 Marks) 
28 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
DIRECT TAX LAWS & INTERNATIONAL TAXATION

parts.answer_text:
(ii)  1. 
Tax Planning – Gifting of fixed deposits of ` 50 lakhs by Mr. D to 
his son who attained the age of 18 years for the purpose of 
shifting interest income from his hands to his son so that there 
may be zero tax implication, is a permitted tax planning measure 
under the provisions of income-tax law. 
Note – It has been assumed that such transfer is irrevocable and 
Mr. D does not derive any direct or indirect benefit from such 
income. In case transfer of fixed deposit is revocable then the 
interest income on fixed deposits would be included in the hands of 
Mr. D and hence the same would not be considered as Tax 
Planning.  
29 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
FINAL EXAMINATION: MAY 2024 
2. 
Tax Evasion – Mr. Ram’s annual income is ` 49.50 lakhs for the 
A.Y. 2024-25. He also earned commission of ` 6 lakhs from ABC 
Limited. Accordingly, his total income would be ` 55.50 lakhs 
which exceeds ` 50 lakhs and hence surcharge is applicable on 
tax on total income.  
However, for the purpose of saving tax, he instructed ABC Ltd. to 
transfer the commission in his wife’s account. This is the case of 
application of income and not of diversion of income by 
overriding title, since such transfer of commission is not under 
any obligation but to evade tax.   
This is tax evasion.

(a) (i)  Form 15CB is a certificate of an accountant wherein he certifies that 
he has examined the agreement between the remitter and the 
beneficiary requiring such remittance he has examined also the 
relevant documents and books of account required for ascertaining 
the nature of remittance and for determining the rate of deduction of 
tax at source.   
The Chartered Accountant certifying the Form 15CB undertakes to 
have verified the agreement between the remitter and the beneficiary 
as well as the relevant documents and books of account to ascertain 
the nature of remittance and determine the rate of TDS.  
In this case, however, the Chartered Accountant mentioned that he 
had only verified KYC of signatory to invoice and the invoices thereof.   
He had not only failed to justify as to how verification of invoices was 
considered as sufficient compliance for certifying the forms but also 
failed to bring on record the said invoices.   
Thus, he failed to provide any basis on which he relied for issuing 
Form 15CB certificates to the company. 
On account of such failure, clauses (7) and (8) of Part I of the Second 
Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 for failure to 
exercise due diligence in discharging his professional responsibilities 
and failure to obtain sufficient information may be invoked.

(b)  Application for Advance Ruling 
As per section 245R, the Board for Advance Rulings (BAR), after examining 
the application and the records called for, may either allow or reject an 
application. However, the Board shall not allow an application where the 
question raised in the application is already pending before any income-
tax authority, or Appellate Tribunal or any court. 
In the present case, the question raised by a non-resident foreign 
company with respect to tax liability on income arising from installation of 
mobile telephone system is already pending before the Assessing Officer 
on account of application made by one of the Indian Companies for 
determination of question of law with regard to the payments made to 
the said foreign company. 
Since such question is already pending before the Income-tax Authority, 
the rejection of application of the foreign company by the BAR is justified 
in law.  
Alternate Answer 
However, as per the Explanatory Memorandum to the Finance Bill, 2020 
(See Note below) the BAR shall not allow the application only if the 
question raised is already pending in the applicant’s case before any 
income-tax authority.  
Accordingly, based on this view, the rejection of application by the BAR is 
not justified in law, since the question raised in the application made by 
the foreign company is pending before the Assessing Officer in the case 
of one of the Indian Companies, and not in the applicant’s case. 
30 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
DIRECT TAX LAWS & INTERNATIONAL TAXATION 
Note - The first proviso to section 245R(2) has been substituted by the 
Finance Act, 2000 with effect from 1.6.2000. Clause (i) of the first proviso, 
prior to and post amendment, reads as follows: 
Prior to 1.6.2000 
On or After 1.6.2000 
Provided that the Authority shall not 
allow the application except in the case 
of a resident applicant where the 
question raised in the application is 
already pending in the applicant’s case 
before any income-tax authority, the 
Appellate Tribunal or any court; 
Provided that the Authority 
shall not allow the application 
where the question raised in 
the 
application 
is 
already 
pending before any income-
tax authority or Appellate 
Tribunal or any court. 
The words “except in the case of a resident applicant” and “in the 
applicant’s case” has been removed in clause (i) of the first proviso with 
effect from 1.6.2000. However, the Explanatory Memorandum to the 
Finance Act, 2000, explaining the impact of the substitution, reads as 
follows:  
“It is proposed to substitute the proviso to provide that the Authority shall 
not allow the application when the question raised is already pending in 
the applicant’s case before any income-tax authority, Appellate Tribunal 
or any court in regard to a non-resident applicant and resident applicant in 
relation to a transaction with a non-resident”.  
Therefore, according to the intent expressed in the Explanatory 
Memorandum, the AAR shall not allow the application both in the case of 
resident and non-resident applicant if the question raised is already 
pending in the applicant’s case before any income-tax authority.  
Thus, as per the Explanatory Memorandum, it is possible to take a view that 
even post-amendment, the Authority shall not allow the application only 
where a question is pending in the applicant’s case before any income-tax 
authority.  
31
