Raw materials held for business
inclusion: Property of any kind held by an assessee
Securities held by specified Foreign Institutional Investors or investment funds
Unit linked insurance policies without specific exemptions
descriptor.definition: Profits and gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset effected in a tax year are chargeable to income-tax under the head Capital Gains and deemed as income of that specific year. The core elements driving this charge are the identification of a valid capital asset and a recognized transfer.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between items held as business stock-in-trade versus items held as personal investments based on the manner of holding rather than the inherent nature of the asset.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR REGISTERED NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATION
Special Provisions for Registered Non-Profit Organization

exclusion: Commercial business entities operating for profit
Private trusts claiming public charitable exemptions solely by status
inclusion: Trusts, societies, and section 8 companies
Public trusts with general public beneficiaries
Private trusts formed for individual or family convenience
descriptor.definition: Non-profit organizations are typically established as trusts, societies, or section 8 companies to carry out charitable or religious activities. A trust involves an obligation where a trustee holds and manages property according to a trust deed for the benefit of ascertainable or unascertainable beneficiaries.
nearby_distinctions: Public trusts qualify for special charitable exemption regimes, whereas private trusts do not qualify merely by being constituted as a trust.

path.name: Classes and Administrative Structure of Income-Tax Authorities

exclusion: Judicial courts outside the income-tax department hierarchy
Non-statutory bodies without administrative linkage
inclusion: Central Board of Direct Taxes
Directorate ranks
Commissioner ranks
Assessing Officers including ACIT, DCIT, and authorized ITOs
descriptor.definition: The Income-tax Act establishes a hierarchical administrative machinery headed by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, followed by various classes of directors-general, chief commissioners, commissioners, and subordinate officers. The CBDT functions under the Ministry of Finance to exercise statutory control, supervise the department, and frame necessary rules for proper administration.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from appellate dispute resolution panels and general civil courts by operating purely within the direct tax administrative machinery.

exclusion: Loss returns
Returns decreasing total tax liability
Returns creating or increasing refunds
Cases involving search, requisition, or certain surveys
inclusion: Returns filed within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year
Returns furnishing additional income
descriptor.definition: Assessees can furnish an updated return for any previous year within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, regardless of whether original, belated, or revised returns were previously filed. However, updated returns are prohibited if they report a loss, decrease tax liability, result in or increase refunds, or if search, survey, or related proceedings apply.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from belated returns under section 139(4) and revised returns under section 139(5) by its specific purpose of updating income with additional tax payments and strict non-applicability to loss or refund scenarios.

path.name: Specified class or classes of persons to be exempted from filing return of income [Section 139(1C)]
Specified Class Or Classes Of Persons To Be Exempted From Filing Return Of Income [Section 139(1C)]

exclusion: Taxpayers earning other Indian-sourced incomes outside the specified exemptions
inclusion: Non-corporate non-residents with fund income in IFSC
Foreign companies with fund income in IFSC
descriptor.definition: The Central Government may exempt specific classes of taxpayers from filing a return of income to minimize compliance burdens. This includes non-corporate non-residents and foreign companies whose sole Indian income derives from specified International Financial Services Centre investment funds subject to tax deduction at source.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard filing requirements by granting total exemption from submitting returns under section 139(1) via executive notification.

path.name: MODE OF TAKING OR ACCEPTING CERTAIN LOANS, DEPOSITS AND SPECIFIED SUM [SECTION 269SS]
Mode Of Taking Or Accepting Certain Loans, Deposits And Specified Sum [Section 269Ss]

exclusion: Transactions involving the Government or banking companies
Transactions where parties derive income solely from agriculture
Transactions where neither party has taxable income
inclusion: Loans or deposits of 20,000 rupees or more
Unpaid earlier loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Specified sums receivable for immovable property transfers
descriptor.definition: Accepting loans, deposits, or specified sums equal to or exceeding 20,000 rupees must be executed through account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. Specified sums include advance monies receivable regarding immovable property transfers, subject to specific institutional exemptions and agricultural conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269T which governs loan repayments rather than acceptance
Differs from Section 269ST which governs general daily or transactional cash receipt limits

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: payments made to the Government
payments made to specified banking companies or co-operative societies
inclusion: cash payments exceeding 1 crore rupees generally
cash payments exceeding 20 lakhs rupees for non-filers of returns
descriptor.definition: Banking institutions, co-operative banks, and post offices must deduct tax at source on cash withdrawals exceeding specific statutory thresholds during a previous year. Higher tax rates and lower withdrawal limits apply to recipients who have failed to file income tax returns for the preceding three assessment years.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard payment-based TDS provisions by targeting physical cash withdrawals from bank accounts based on aggregate annual volume.

path.name: PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]
PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]

exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
descriptor.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction only one mode of recovery [Section 202]
Deduction Only One Mode Of Recovery [Section 202]

exclusion: Exclusive reliance on withholding tax mechanisms for tax recovery
inclusion: Utilization of other recovery modes alongside TDS
descriptor.definition: Tax deduction at source represents solely one method available for recovering tax obligations. The Assessing Officer retains the statutory authority to deploy any alternative recovery mechanisms prescribed by law.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the bar against direct demand by ensuring recovery powers remain broad and unrestricted by the mere existence of TDS.

exclusion: Personal attendance ordered under section 131 for examination on oath or affirmation
inclusion: Representation before tax authorities for asset valuation
Representation before the Appellate Tribunal for valuation matters
descriptor.definition: Taxpayers are permitted to appear through a registered valuer before any income tax authority or the Appellate Tribunal regarding asset valuation matters. This representation right excludes personal attendance mandates required under section 131 for examination on oath or affirmation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general authorized representation under section 288 by being specifically restricted to valuation proceedings.

path.name: PRESUMPTION AS TO ASSETS, BOOKS OF ACCOUNT, ETC. [SECTION 292C]
Presumption As To Assets, Books Of Account, Etc. [Section 292C]

exclusion: Materials and assets not found in the possession or control of the person during search, survey, or requisition
inclusion: Evidentiary presumptions regarding ownership of seized assets and documents
Assumptions of truth and correct execution for books of account and records
descriptor.definition: Books of account, documents, money, and assets found during searches, surveys, or requisition proceedings are legally presumed to belong to the person in possession. Further presumptions apply that document contents are true, signatures and handwriting belong to the purported authors, and executed documents were duly stamped and executed.
nearby_distinctions: Extends the evidentiary presumptions originally created for search operations to regular assessments and survey proceedings.

context.question_text:
(i) Question paper comprises of 6 questions. Answer Question No. 1 which is 
compulsory and any 4 questions out of the remaining 5 questions.

exclusion: taxable supplies subject to standard or reduced positive rates
supplies outside statutory definitions
inclusion: supplies attracting nil rate of tax
wholly exempt goods or services
non-taxable supplies including specified petroleum products and alcoholic liquor
descriptor.definition: An exempt supply comprises any goods, services, or both attracting a nil tax rate, full exemption, or non-taxable status under governing statutes. This classification includes items and services not leviable to tax under the primary legislative acts.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes between wholly exempt items and non-taxable supplies which are both subsumed under exempt supply definitions

exclusion: Money and securities from general goods definition
inclusion: Movable property
Actionable claims
Activities relating to use of money
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions delineate key terms such as goods, services, principal, family, and local authorities to establish clear statutory boundaries for tax applicability. These definitions remove ambiguities by specifying exact inclusions and exclusions within the legislative framework.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between general movable property and excluded financial instruments like money and securities.

exclusion: immovable property statutory rules for port operations
inclusion: e-commerce delivery address recording
port wagon haulage and unloading services
descriptor.definition: Administrative clarifications resolve specific compliance ambiguities regarding e-commerce deliveries to unregistered persons and port cargo handling services. Cargo operations ancillary to port handling are classified under general service rules rather than immovable property rules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes port cargo handling ancillary operations from direct immovable property leases or construction services.

exclusion: Non-ad-valorem levies
Transactions where price is not the sole consideration
inclusion: Goods and services supply valuations
CGST, SGST, UTGST, and IGST computation frameworks
descriptor.definition: Fiscal statutes compute tax liability on an ad-valorem basis using a prescribed valuation mechanism for goods and services. The transaction value between unrelated parties acts as the default taxable base under statutory valuation provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard transaction value pricing from specialized rule-based valuation methods used when standard criteria fail.
instrument_references: Chapter IV of the CGST Rules, 2017

path.name: CHANGE IN RATE OF TAX IN RESPECT OF SUPPLY OF GOODS OR SERVICES [SECTION 14]
Time of Supply under Change in Rate of Tax

exclusion: Standard forward charge time of supply without rate changes
Reverse charge mechanics
inclusion: Supplies made before tax rate change
Supplies made after tax rate change
descriptor.definition: When tax rates change, the time of supply overrides standard provisions to depend strictly on the chronological relationship between the date of supply, invoice issuance, and payment receipt. Specific permutations dictate whether the supply occurs before or after the rate revision.
nearby_distinctions: Applies specialized ordering rules based on rate change timing rather than standard invoice or payment precedence

path.name: POWER TO GRANT EXEMPTION FROM TAX [SECTION 11 OF THE CGST ACT/SECTION 6 OF THE IGST ACT]
Power to Grant Exemption from Tax

exclusion: collection of tax in excess of effective rates on absolute exemptions
exemptions granted without council recommendation
inclusion: general exemptions via notification
special orders for exceptional circumstances
explanations inserted within one year to clarify scope
descriptor.definition: The Government may issue notifications or special orders on council recommendations to exempt specific goods or services from whole or part of taxes in the public interest. Registered suppliers must not collect tax exceeding the effective rate on absolutely exempted supplies.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes general notifications applied broadly from special orders issued for exceptional individual cases

path.name: LEVY & COLLECTION OF CGST & IGST [SECTION 9 OF THE CGST ACT & SECTION 5 OF THE IGST ACT]
Levy and Collection of CGST and IGST

exclusion: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption
Un-denatured extra neutral alcohol or rectified spirit used for manufacturing alcoholic liquor
inclusion: All intra-State supplies of goods or services under CGST
All inter-State supplies of goods or services under IGST
descriptor.definition: Central goods and services tax and integrated goods and services tax are levied on all intra-State and inter-State supplies respectively, subject to specified statutory exceptions and notification timelines. Tax liability may be shifted to the recipient under reverse charge mechanisms for specified categories of goods or services.
nearby_distinctions: Standard forward charge places liability on the supplier, whereas reverse charge shifts payment obligations directly to the recipient.

exclusion: Time of supply rules for goods
Tax rate change provisions
inclusion: Forward charge rules for services
Reverse charge rules for services
descriptor.definition: The time of supply for services is generally determined as the earliest of the invoice issue date or payment receipt, provided the invoice is issued within the prescribed period. Under reverse charge mechanisms, it relies on payment dates or sixty days from the supplier's invoice.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from goods by incorporating the exact date of service provision and recipient book entries when standard rules fail

path.name: SUPPLIES IN TERRITORIAL WATERS [SECTION 9 OF THE IGST ACT]

exclusion: high seas supplies beyond territorial water limits not captured by baseline rules
inclusion: bunker fuel supplies to vessels
ship stores provided offshore
descriptor.definition: Legal fictions assign supplier locations or places of supply occurring within territorial waters to the nearest coastal baseline state or union territory. This ensures every maritime supply links correctly to a destination-based administrative jurisdiction.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes unassigned offshore maritime locations from land jurisdictions by legally anchoring them to the nearest coastal baseline point.
instrument_references: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act 1976

path.name: INTER-STATE SUPPLY [SECTION 7 OF THE IGST ACT]

exclusion: intra-state supplies within the same state boundary
inclusion: supplies across different state boundaries
imported goods prior to customs clearance crossing
exports outside India
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions classify transactions as inter-state trade when the supplier and place of supply lie in different states or union territories, or involve cross-border imports and exports. Transactions involving Special Economic Zone developers or units are similarly integrated into this framework.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes intra-state supplies occurring strictly within one state from inter-state transactions spanning multiple states, territories, or international borders.

path.name: PLACE OF SUPPLY OF SERVICES WHERE LOCATION OF SUPPLIER OF SERVICE AND THE LOCATION OF THE RECIPIENT OF SERVICE IS IN INDIA [SECTION 12]
Place of Supply of Services Within India

exclusion: cross-border import of services
cross-border export of services
inclusion: architect and interior decorator services
hotel and boat lodging accommodations
event organization at immovable properties
descriptor.definition: Domestic service rules establish the place of supply based on recipient registration status or specific performance ties to immovable properties and venues. Properties spanning multiple territories require proportional value allocation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general B2B and B2C recipient-location rules from location-specific performance rules governing immovable property and related events.

path.name: GST Foundation and Territorial Charging Mechanism

exclusion: Supplies outside the charging provisions of the respective tax statutes
inclusion: Intra-State supplies of goods or services
Inter-State supplies of goods or services
descriptor.definition: The charge of goods and services tax is triggered by the taxable event of supply, drawing its legislative power from the Constitution of India. Intra-State supplies attract central tax and state or union territory tax, whereas inter-State supplies attract integrated tax.
nearby_distinctions: Intra-State supply is governed by CGST and SGST/UTGST based on supplier location and place of supply, whereas inter-State supply attracts IGST.

exclusion: Central and State Government subsidies
Discounts recorded on invoices or linked via pre-supply agreements with reversed ITC
inclusion: Separate third-party levies other than specified GST laws
Recipient liabilities paid by supplier
Delayed payment interest, late fees, and penalties
descriptor.definition: The taxable value of a supply equals its transaction value when parties are unrelated and price is the sole consideration. Additions such as incidental expenses, recipient liabilities, non-government subsidies, and taxes are included, while qualifying pre- and post-supply discounts are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts mandatory additions to the price with permitted exclusions like conditional discounts and government subsidies.

path.name: PLACE OF SUPPLY OF GOODS OTHER THAN SUPPLY OF GOODS IMPORTED INTO, OR EXPORTED FROM INDIA [SECTION 10]
Place of Supply of Domestic Goods

exclusion: imported goods cross-border transactions
exported goods leaving India
inclusion: terminating points of goods movement
third-party principal business locations
unregistered consumer invoice addresses
descriptor.definition: Statutory rules determine the location where domestic goods are supplied based on physical movement, third-party delivery directions, or stationary delivery. For unregistered recipients, specific invoicing address criteria apply when movement is absent.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard movement-based delivery rules from bill-to-ship-to triangular arrangements where a third party's principal place of business dictates the outcome.

path.name: Statutory Definitions for Time of Supply

exclusion: Substantive charging sections
Operational assessment procedures
inclusion: Definition of movable property and actionable claims
Definition of services including money conversion activities
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions establish legal meanings for terms such as associated enterprises, documents, invoices, goods, services, and reverse charge mechanisms. These definitions provide the necessary foundation for interpreting time of supply provisions across transactions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between physical goods and intangible services or actionable claims

path.name: Relevant Definitions for Place of Supply

exclusion: valuation mechanisms
time of supply triggers
inclusion: conveyance classifications
distinct person establishment rules
foreign exchange receipt conditions
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions establish legal boundaries for continuous passenger journeys, international trade movements, and organizational establishments. These terms govern the interpretation of cross-border and multi-location transactions under the GST framework.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between a regular place of business and a fixed establishment based on the sufficiency of human and technical resources.

exclusion: Historical events like manufacture or separate sale
Transactions involving money and securities
inclusion: Supply of goods
Supply of services
descriptor.definition: Supply serves as the single comprehensive taxable event replacing prior fragmented triggers like manufacture, sale, and service provision. It dictates the precise threshold at which tax liability arises across the integrated tax framework.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from previous regime events by integrating manufacture and sale into a single unified supply concept.

path.name: CONCEPT OF SUPPLY [SECTION 7 OF THE CGST ACT]
Concept of Supply [Section 7 of the CGST Act]

exclusion: Activities specified in Schedule III
Transactions explicitly excluded from the scope of supply
inclusion: Sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal
Importation of services for consideration
Activities specified in Schedule I without consideration
descriptor.definition: Supply encompasses forms of goods or services transactions made for consideration in the course of business, specific member-entity activities, import of services, and specified transactions without consideration. The statutory schedules further classify these transactions as supplies of goods or services or exclude them entirely.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard commercial supplies from non-consideration supplies under Schedule I and excluded activities under Schedule III.

path.name: INTRA-STATE SUPPLY [SECTION 8 OF THE IGST ACT]

exclusion: Special Economic Zone developer or unit supplies
imported goods before customs clearance
inclusion: supplies within the same state
branch establishments treated as distinct persons
descriptor.definition: Intra-state supply occurs when both the supplier and the place of supply are located within the same state or union territory, attracting CGST and SGST. Specific transactions involving Special Economic Zone units, uncrossed imports, or international tourists are legally excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard local state-contained transactions from excluded categories like SEZ supplies that default to inter-state treatment despite occurring locally.

exclusion: processed or branded items outside the exemption notification
taxable manufactured goods
inclusion: unbranded or unpackaged staple food items
fresh milk, eggs, and curd
fresh vegetables and specified raw agricultural produce
descriptor.definition: Specified everyday consumption items are exempted from the whole of tax under statutory exemption powers. These include essential public consumption products notified under governing tax legislation.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes raw or unpackaged essential food items from processed commercial goods subject to standard taxation

path.name: LIST OF SERVICES EXEMPT FROM TAX
List of Services Exempt From Tax

exclusion: renting of rooms with daily charges meeting or exceeding specified monetary thresholds
renting of commercial shops exceeding monthly rental limits
inclusion: charitable activities by registered entities
religious ceremonies and eligible renting of religious precincts
training or coaching in arts, culture, or sports by specified entities
descriptor.definition: Specific categories of services rendered by qualified entities, such as charitable activities and religious ceremonies, are exempted wholly from central tax under designated notifications. Certain monetary thresholds apply to determine the applicability of exemptions on renting properties and premises.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes general commercial service providers from charitable trusts and religious institutions qualifying for specific service exemptions

exclusion: Money and securities from the definitions of goods and services
inclusion: Movable property, actionable claims, and specified growing crops
Value of taxable, exempt, export, and inter-state supplies for aggregate turnover
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions provide precise meanings for key terms such as goods, services, aggregate turnover, and reverse charge under the tax statutes. These definitions establish the operational boundaries and tax liabilities for various transactions and entities.
nearby_distinctions: Aggregate turnover is computed on an all-India basis excluding specific central, state, and integrated taxes, unlike standard turnover measures.

path.name: Time of Supply Framework for Goods and Services

exclusion: Due dates for payment of tax
Detailed tax invoice rules
inclusion: Point of tax liability determination
Provisions for goods and services
descriptor.definition: The time of supply indicates the exact point when the liability to pay goods and services tax arises for intra-State or inter-State transactions. While the tax liability crystallizes at this specific time, the actual payment can be made by the prescribed due dates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the payment of tax due date which occurs later in the filing cycle

exclusion: Time of supply rules for services
Tax rate change provisions
inclusion: Forward charge supply rules for goods
Reverse charge supply rules for goods
descriptor.definition: The time of supply for goods is determined as the earliest of the invoice issue date, the last date required for invoice issuance, or the date of payment receipt. For reverse charge supplies, specific alternative rules apply involving goods receipt, payment entry, or thirty days post-invoice.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from service rules by prioritizing delivery milestones and different reverse charge timelines

path.name: RULES FOR VALUATION OF SUPPLY OF GOODS AND/OR SERVICES

exclusion: Standard arm-length transactions where price is the sole monetary consideration under section 15(1)
inclusion: Barter transactions
Part-exchange arrangements
Supplies between distinct establishments or related entities
descriptor.definition: Valuation rules determine taxable values when consideration is not wholly in money or when transactions occur between distinct or related persons. The process follows a hierarchical methodology starting with open market value and falling back to like-kind quality or computed cost rules.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates default transaction pricing from sequential fallback valuation rules applied during non-monetary or related-party transactions.

path.name: PLACE OF SUPPLY OF GOODS IMPORTED INTO, OR EXPORTED FROM INDIA [SECTION 11]
Place of Supply for Cross-Border Goods

exclusion: domestic intrastate transactions
inter-state domestic movements
inclusion: importer location indexing
destination outside India tagging
descriptor.definition: Cross-border supply rules designate the importer's location as the place of supply for incoming goods and foreign destinations for outgoing goods. These cross-border transactions are classified as inter-state and zero-rated where applicable.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes domestic supply movement termination rules from international trade criteria tied strictly to import boundaries and foreign export destinations.

exclusion: Government subsidies
Deposits held without supplier application
Money and securities
inclusion: Mercantile agents and brokers
Monetary and non-monetary payments
Actionable claims and growing crops
Dependent family members
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions establish specific legal meanings for agents, consideration, family dependents, goods, and market value within the indirect tax framework. Deposits are excluded from consideration unless explicitly applied by the supplier as payment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes held security deposits from active payment consideration based on supplier application timing.

path.name: Extent and Commencement of GST Law

exclusion: Territories outside the specified sovereign boundaries of India
inclusion: Territory of India under Article 1 of the Constitution
Maritime zones including territorial waters and exclusive economic zones
descriptor.definition: The tax statutes extend to the entire territory of India, encompassing its territorial waters, seabed, subsoil, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and designated airspace. Each respective state or union territory enactment applies within its defined geographical boundaries.
nearby_distinctions: CGST and IGST extend pan-India, whereas UTGST applies exclusively to specific union territories without legislatures.
instrument_references: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976

exclusion: tax computation rules
input tax credit claiming mechanics
inclusion: goods consumption locations
service delivery tracking
cross-state service flows
descriptor.definition: The place of supply identifies the consumption jurisdiction for destination-based taxation, establishing where tax revenue must accrue. It resolves complexities caused by the intangible nature of services, mobile recipients, and alterable delivery formats.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the physical location of the supplier or billing address by focusing strictly on the ultimate place of consumption.

path.name: POWER NOT TO RECOVER GOODS AND SERVICES TAX NOT LEVIED OR SHORT- LEVIED AS A RESULT OF GENERAL PRACTICE
Power Not to Recover Tax Not Levied or Short-Levied Due to General Practice

exclusion: tax non-payment resulting from isolated taxpayer errors unsupported by general trade practice
adjustments executed without council recommendation
inclusion: supplies where central tax was not levied due to prevalent general practice
supplies charged at a lower rate in accordance with established industry customs
descriptor.definition: The Government may direct that uncollected or short-levied tax need not be paid if a specific industry practice of non-levy or lower levy was generally prevalent. This relief mechanism protects taxpayers who followed widespread customary practices in good faith upon council recommendations.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes regular statutory exemptions from retroactive relief granted specifically for widespread industry misinterpretations or customary practices

path.name: COMPOSITION LEVY [SECTION 10 OF THE CGST ACT]

exclusion: Taxpayers engaged in inter-State outward supplies of goods or services
Suppliers of non-taxable goods or services
inclusion: Registered persons with preceding financial year aggregate turnover meeting statutory limits
Manufacturers, restaurant service providers, and other eligible suppliers
descriptor.definition: Eligible registered taxpayers with an aggregate turnover below a specified statutory threshold in the preceding financial year may opt to pay tax at a concessional rate calculated on their state or union territory turnover. This scheme restricts outward inter-State supplies and limits the supply of services alongside specific manufacturing or catering conditions.
terminology: Turnover in State or Union territory
nearby_distinctions: Composition levy offers a simplified tax calculation at lower rates based on state turnover instead of standard rates, subject to strict eligibility constraints.

exclusion: Unbundled individual supplies evaluated separately
inclusion: Naturally bundled supplies dependent on a principal supply
Unrelated supplies bundled together for a single price
descriptor.definition: Composite supplies involving naturally bundled elements take the tax rate of their principal supply, whereas mixed supplies not naturally bundled attract the highest applicable tax rate among their components. This mechanism ensures taxation certainty for bundled transactions combining multiple goods or services.
nearby_distinctions: Composite supplies rely on natural bundling and a principal component, while mixed supplies lack natural bundling and attract the highest tax rate.

M/s. YVPAY Bank Ltd. had opted for optional method, under section 17(4) of

parts.question_text:
(i) Mr. Anil utilized the amount of ` 2,500 from the master wallet towards 
playing a virtual racing game on the portal. As a winning amount  
` 11,000 was credited to the master wallet of Mr. Anil.

parts.label: ii
parts.question_text:
(ii) On another portal operated by M/s Win here 2407 in the name of Win 
90, Mr. Anil placed a bet of face value of ` 12,000 on an international 
cricket match. The amount of such bet was paid through the master 
wallet with applicable taxes and accordingly, the bet amount of ` 12,000 
with applicable taxes was transferred from the master wallet of Mr. Anil 
to the bank account of Win 90. However, he lost the bet.

parts.label: iii
parts.question_text:
(iii) Mr. Anil transferred the balance amount from the master wallet to his 
bank account after doing the aforesaid transactions.  
Based on the information provided above, answer the following questions, 
providing reasons in brief: 
(1) Compute the taxable value under GST law and total GST payable on the 
aforesaid given transactions in the hands of M/s Win here 2407 in India.  
(2) Determine the net amount transferred by Mr. Anil from the master wallet 
to his bank account after the aforesaid transactions.  
Note: 
Assume all the above transactions to be exclusive of GST unless otherwise 
specified. Rate of GST applicable is 28% (ignore the bifurcation of GST 
amount into CGST and SGST or IGST). Calculate amount of value and tax 
rounded off to nearest rupee.  
(5 Marks)

(b) M/s. Win here 2407 is an online money gaming platform operating from 
Singapore. It provides its users a platform to play and win money in different 
games etc. that are available on its web portal.   
In the month of October 2023, Mr. Anil (player), an unregistered person

inclusion: sum paid or credited for purchasing goods exceeding 50 lakhs rupees in a previous year
buyers with business turnover exceeding 10 crores rupees in the preceding financial year
descriptor.definition: Large business buyers whose preceding financial year turnover exceeds specified monetary limits must deduct tax at source when purchasing goods from a resident seller exceeding aggregate thresholds. The deduction occurs at the time of credit to the seller's account or actual payment, whichever happens earlier.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from TCS provisions under section 206C(1H) by placing the compliance burden directly on the high-turnover buyer rather than the seller.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
Mandatory Tax Audit Provisions and Thresholds

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits in accordance with section 44AD(1) or 44ADA(1)
inclusion: Businesses with total sales exceeding specific statutory limits
Professions with gross receipts exceeding fifty lakh rupees
Assessees claiming lower profits than presumptive rates under designated sections
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professions must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date when financial metrics cross prescribed monetary thresholds. Exceptions and specific conditions regarding cash receipts and payments apply to business turnovers within defined limits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes business turnover thresholds from professional gross receipt thresholds and presumptive income reporting rules.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Understanding relationship between the reporting entity and another entity/entities
Relationship Between Reporting Entity and Other Entities

exclusion: Entities linked merely by a shared common director without additional control or significant influence
inclusion: Fellow subsidiaries and group parents
Joint ventures and associates
Post-employment benefit plans for employees
descriptor.definition: An entity is related to a reporting entity if they are group members, associates, joint ventures, or controlled by the same person. Additional links include post-employment benefit plans and entities providing key management personnel services.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes structural corporate affiliations and shared control frameworks from casual operational partnerships.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors
COMPANY TO HAVE BOARD OF DIRECTORS [SECTION 149]

exclusion: Non-individual entities such as bodies corporate, firms, or association of persons
Exceeding 15 directors without passing a special resolution
inclusion: Minimum director requirements for public companies, private companies, and OPCs
Appointment of at least one woman director for prescribed classes of companies
descriptor.definition: Every company must constitute a Board of Directors consisting solely of individuals, adhering to specified minimum and maximum numerical thresholds. Public companies require a minimum of three directors, private companies two, and One Person Companies one, with an overall maximum cap of fifteen unless expanded via special resolution.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general member composition by strictly mandating individual natural persons and setting specific structural minimums and maximums.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 3

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Classification of Cash Flows as Investing Activity
Classification of Cash Flows as Investing Activity

exclusion: Financing transactions involving partial equity changes without loss of control
Standard operating cycle cash flows
inclusion: Total consideration paid or received for control changes
Cash and cash equivalents acquired or disposed of in business changes
descriptor.definition: Aggregate cash flows arising from acquiring or relinquishing control of subsidiaries or other businesses are classified strictly as investing activities and presented separately. The net cash consideration paid or received is reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired or disposed of in the transaction.
nearby_distinctions: Separates major structural entity acquisition or disposal cash flows from routine operational or financing cash movements.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Connections lacking substantive economic or operational control, joint control, or significant influence
inclusion: Relationships between reporting entity and individuals
Relationships between reporting entity and other corporate entities
descriptor.definition: A related party is a person or entity connected to the reporting entity, where evaluation must prioritize the substance of the relationship over mere legal form. Relationships involve either person-to-entity connections or entity-to-entity connections.
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes underlying economic substance and control rather than strictly formal legal categorization.

exclusion: Treating the entity being taken over as the acquirer in standard direct combinations
inclusion: Application of purchase method principles to the acquiree's net assets
Evaluation of control indicators beyond basic voting percentages
descriptor.definition: The acquiring enterprise is defined as the entity that secures control over the acquiree, triggering the application of the acquisition method of accounting. Identifying this entity involves assessing control frameworks and reviewing governance indicators such as board control and potential voting rights.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from the acquiree by being the sole entity possessing power to direct relevant activities and generate variable returns

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Agreements lacking an identified asset or failing to grant asset use direction rights
inclusion: Contracts granting rights to use explicitly or implicitly specified assets with economic benefit control
descriptor.definition: A contract is or contains a lease if it conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration. This assessment is performed at the inception date, defined as the earlier of the lease agreement date or the date of commitment to principal terms.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes pure service contracts from lease arrangements based on control over the underlying asset use

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Disclosure requirements in other Ind AS
Disclosure Requirements In Other Ind As

exclusion: Direct standard-specific disclosures covered entirely within Ind AS 19
inclusion: Related party transactions with post-employment benefit plans
Contingent liabilities from post-employment benefit obligations
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide disclosures concerning post-employment benefit plans and key management personnel under separate accounting standards. Additionally, disclosures regarding contingent liabilities arising from employee benefit obligations are required.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard-internal disclosures by relying strictly on external standard mandates like Ind AS 24 and Ind AS 37.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits on a presumptive basis unless claiming lower than deemed profits
inclusion: Businesses with total sales or turnover exceeding 1 crore or 10 crore depending on cash transaction proportions
Professionals with gross receipts exceeding 50 lakhs
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professionals must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date if their turnover or gross receipts exceed statutory monetary limits. An audit report in the prescribed form must be duly signed and verified.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general maintenance of books of account by requiring formal verification and reporting by an external accountant.

path.name: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL AUDITORS
Relationship Between Internal And External Auditors

exclusion: Delegating the statutory auditor's ultimate legal opinion responsibility entirely to internal personnel
inclusion: Evaluating internal audit staff qualifications and department structure
Assessing internal control reliability for external audit reliance
Modifying external audit testing intensity based on internal evaluations
descriptor.definition: The statutory auditor must examine the scope, effectiveness, and independence of the internal audit function to determine its impact on external audit procedures. While internal and external audit scopes often overlap, statutory auditors evaluate internal audit work to appropriately adjust the nature, timing, and extent of their compliance and substantive testing.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the external auditor's primary focus on financial statement attestation versus the internal auditor's ongoing internal governance and operational focus.

path.name: CARO 2020 Additional Reporting Framework and Applicability

exclusion: Banking and insurance company inclusion
Consolidated financial statement applicability
inclusion: Additional reporting for qualifying corporations
Exemption evaluations for small and private companies
descriptor.definition: Issued under statutory authority, the order mandates additional reporting disclosures for eligible companies alongside the primary audit report. Specific entity types, such as banking companies, insurance entities, and small companies meeting specific criteria, are exempt from these extra requirements.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as an supplementary reporting order rather than the standard financial statement audit opinion.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Understanding relationship between the reporting entity and a person(s)
Relationship Between Reporting Entity and Persons

exclusion: Ordinary employees without management authority or significant ownership influence
inclusion: Individuals holding control or joint control
Individuals exercising significant influence
Key management personnel of the reporting entity or its parent
descriptor.definition: An individual or their close family member is related to a reporting entity if they hold control, joint control, or significant influence over it. Such relationship also arises if the individual serves as key management personnel for the reporting entity or its parent.
nearby_distinctions: Restricts personal related-party status to individuals holding designated governance, management, or ownership powers.

exclusion: Personal attendance required under section 131
Auditor-disqualified individuals acting as company accountants
inclusion: Written authorization for legal and financial representation
Qualified accountants and legal practitioners acting on behalf of assessees
descriptor.definition: Assessees may attend proceedings before income tax authorities or the Appellate Tribunal through a written authorized representative. Eligible representatives include relatives, regular employees, scheduled bank officers, legal practitioners, and qualified chartered accountants meeting specific independence criteria.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike registered valuers who focus solely on valuation, authorized representatives can handle general proceedings under the Act.

exclusion: Appointed or formal dates specified in agreements where control has not yet transferred
inclusion: Date of obtaining control over board representation or operating policies
Dates specified by written agreements transferring control prior to legal closing
descriptor.definition: The acquisition date is the precise point when the acquirer obtains control over the acquiree, which typically aligns with the closing date of legal transfer. Contractual provisions can shift this date earlier or later depending on when actual operational and financial control is secured.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from legal transfer dates or arbitrary appointed dates by strictly depending on the transfer of power and control

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

exclusion: Non-cash asset acquisitions via equity issuance
Bonus share issues involving no cash flows
inclusion: Proceeds from issuing shares or equity instruments
Proceeds and repayments of debentures, loans, and bonds
Lease liability payments by lessees
descriptor.definition: Financing activities encompass cash flows resulting from changes in the size and composition of an entity's contributed equity and borrowings. These flows assist in predicting future claims on capital providers by capturing fund-raising, capital redemption, and associated capital costs.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from investing activities by focusing on capital structure adjustments rather than long-term asset acquisitions.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A

PROVISION FOR PROFESSIONAL ASSISTANCE TO COMPANY LIQUIDATOR [SECTION 291]

inclusion: Appointment of qualified professionals with tribunal approval
Mandatory disclosure of conflict of interest or independence gaps
descriptor.definition: The company liquidator may engage chartered accountants, company secretaries, cost accountants, or legal practitioners with tribunal sanction to assist in discharging duties. Appointed professionals must immediately disclose any conflicts of interest or lack of independence.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on hiring external professional experts rather than utilizing internal company officers or advisory committees.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Unit 5: THE ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: Items failing to meet the three core criteria of right, benefit potential, and entity control
inclusion: Rights to receive cash, goods, or services
Rights over physical objects and intellectual property
Constructive obligations of other parties
descriptor.definition: An asset is defined as a present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events, where an economic resource represents a right with the potential to produce economic benefits. These rights can arise from counterparties' obligations, physical objects, intellectual property, contracts, or statutory legislation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from mere expenditure, as spending money does not automatically guarantee the acquisition of an asset.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Financial assets under Ind AS 32
Exploration and evaluation assets under Ind AS 106
Mineral development and extraction expenditures
inclusion: Computer software not integral to hardware
Licences and patents
descriptor.definition: The standard applies to all intangible assets except those explicitly scoped out, such as financial assets, exploration and evaluation assets, and mineral extraction expenditures. Items incorporating both tangible and intangible elements require professional judgment to determine the more significant component.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standalone intangible software and software that is an integral part of hardware governed by Ind AS 16.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999

exclusion: Individuals staying abroad for employment, business, or uncertain duration despite physical presence thresholds
inclusion: Individuals residing in India for more than 182 days in the preceding year
Entities registered or incorporated in India
Domestic and foreign owned corporate branches
descriptor.definition: Residential status under this statute depends on physical presence in India exceeding 182 days during the preceding financial year. Specific exceptions apply for employment, business, or uncertain stays abroad regardless of citizenship.

path.name: INTERNAL AUDIT AS A MANAGEMENT FUNCTION

inclusion: Evaluation of internal controls

Root cause identification for control weaknesses
descriptor.definition: Internal audit acts as a vital management control mechanism that independently evaluates internal controls and risk management processes. nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from executive management functions by maintaining operational independence while providing objective evaluation and advisory support.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
